# Go further, if you have time

None of this is required. If you have time, watch Alan Becker's short videos on [squash and stretch](asset:becker_squash) and [anticipation](asset:becker_anticipation). They work with any tool.

{{deeper}}

## The craft, on either track

- **Alan Becker, *12 Principles of Animation*.** The first two episodes are exactly this week's material. → [the whole series in one video](asset:becker_12_principles)
- **E. G. Lutz, *Animated Cartoons: How They Are Made* (1920), Chapter II, "The Genesis of Motion-Pictures."** One of the first books ever written about how animation is made. It is free to read and in the public domain. Chapter II is where Muybridge's horse fits into the story. → [read it free on Project Gutenberg](asset:lutz_1920)

## The tool: two tracks, one course

The principles are the course. The tool is your choice, and the free one is the classroom. On the free track you can finish the whole course without buying anything.

**Free track: Grease Pencil, in Blender.** Install Blender 5.2 LTS, which is free and open source. Start a new file from the **2D Animation** template. Then set the frame rate to 24 frames per second. Grease Pencil is Blender's 2D toolset: frame-by-frame drawing, onion skinning, layers, a camera, and sound on the timeline.
→ [download Blender](asset:blender_download) · [manual: Grease Pencil, the quick start](asset:gp_intro) · [manual: workspaces](asset:blender_workspaces) · [manual: where to set the frame rate](asset:blender_format)

**Paid track, optional: Toon Boom Harmony.** Harmony is widely used in TV animation. Its **Harmony Essentials Kick-Start** course is free on Toon Boom's own site, with a free account: three modules, about 2 hours 40 minutes in total. This week goes with **Kick-Start Module 1**, "How to Create and Set Up your Project." The 14-day Harmony trial belongs in Module 7, so its two weeks cover your final piece.
→ [the Kick-Start course](asset:harmony_kickstart) · [Harmony docs: creating a scene](asset:harmony_scene)
